facts.note: This is what 'how many contracts are available at a given price' means on Kalshi: depth on the opposite side of the book.

facts.value: A capped scan saw 5,825 open and 3,825 settled markets, of which 175 open and 202 settled were KXMVE* combos

facts.claim: Volume and open interest are large real numbers on the demo env, and notional_value_dollars is always 1.0000
facts.value: Observed BTC series row: volume_fp 80,178,706, open_interest_fp 26,587,877, last_price_dollars 0.98, notional_value_dollars 1.0000
facts.note: Confirms in data what F-22 states from the schema: notional_value_dollars is 1 for a binary market at any size, so it is useless for ranking. The site uses volume x last price and labels it an estimate.

facts.claim: Demo prices reach 0.98 and 0.94 on large-volume markets
facts.value: KXBTCY-27JAN0100-B47500 last 0.98; KXAAAGASM-26MAR31-4.00 last 0.94

facts.claim: A market's result is set when it is determined; payout happens when it is finalized
facts.value: Statuses closed -> determined (result set to yes/no/scalar; settlement timer runs) -> finalized (positions paid; settlement_ts populated). REST settled = finalized.
facts.note: Read 2026-11-20. scripts/simulate.py settles a paper position only on a yes or no result in the collector's settled list. A disputed market can be re-determined (disputed, amended).

facts.claim: Yes/no settlement pays $1 per net contract to the holders of the winning side
facts.value: Yes outcome: yes holders receive $1 per contract. No outcome: no holders receive $1 per contract.
facts.note: Read 2026-11-20. Basis for the payoff used by scripts/simulate.py (payoff 1.00 minus entry minus entry fee). Same page: fees are zero for simple yes/no determinations.

facts.note: Read 2026-11-20. Empty books in the collector's liquidity block must not be read as 'no liquidity' without this check.

facts.claim: GET /markets responses include volume_24h_fp (contracts traded in the last 24h), a fixed-point string — used by the alert model's volume factor
facts.value: volume_24h_fp (string, fixed-point, e.g. "10.00")
facts.how: Read the Get Markets response schema on docs.kalshi.com; the field appears in the documented response body.

facts.claim: GET /markets/orderbooks takes `tickers` as a REPEATED query parameter (string[], 1-100 elements, max 200 chars each), unlike GET /markets, which takes a comma-separated list
facts.value: GET /markets/orderbooks?tickers=A&tickers=B  (NOT ?tickers=A%2CB)
facts.how: Read the parameter spec on the official endpoint page (Required array length 1-100; Maximum string length 200), then both forms were issued against the official demo API on 2026-11-20: https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2/markets/orderbooks?tickers=KXAAAGASM-26DEC31-3.30&tickers=KXBTCY-27JAN0100-B47500 returned both books, while https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2/markets/orderbooks?tickers=KXAAAGASM-26DEC31-3.30%2CKXBTCY-27JAN0100-B47500 returned HTTP 200 with ONE entry whose ticker was the whole joined string and both arrays empty. GET /markets?tickers=A%2CB by contrast returned both markets, so the two endpoints genuinely differ. Empty-vs-unknown behaviour is documented at https://docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/orderbook_responses (a ticker that does not match any market returns 200 with empty arrays, not 404).

facts.claim: Placing any order requires a signed request (an API key); the public demo market-data endpoints do not
facts.value: Order creation POSTs to /portfolio/events/orders with KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY, KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE and KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP headers. Public GET /markets needs none.
facts.how: Read the official quick start this session: Step 1 uses a bare requests.get on .../markets?limit=1&status=open ('no auth required for public market data'); Step 2 builds a signed POST to /portfolio/events/orders. Combined with https://docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/api_keys, which states every trading request must be signed. This is why automated order placement in this project needs a key a human must create (F-07), while every price, alert and paper-trade number on the site does not.

facts.claim: A newly created Kalshi API key is Ed25519 by default; RSA-PSS with SHA-256 is the alternative
facts.value: Ed25519 (PKCS#8, 64-byte signature) is selected by default. RSA 2048-bit with RSA-PSS/SHA-256 is for clients limited to RSA-PSS, including SDKs before 3.31.0.
facts.how: Read the key-types table this session. The executor scripts/kalshi_client.py detects the parsed key type and signs Ed25519 or RSA-PSS accordingly, so either key type works; the timestamp must be within 30 s of Kalshi's clock and the signature covers timestamp+method+path WITHOUT query parameters, both as documented there.

facts.claim: GET /markets responses are cached server-side and can lag the exchange by several seconds
facts.value: 'Responses are cached for a short time, so prices, sizes and status can lag the exchange by several seconds, and filtered listings can lag longer than a read of a single market.' The docs point to the WebSocket API for current state.
facts.how: Read verbatim in the official Get Markets description this session. Consequence for this project: a browser poll is near-real-time, not tick-level, and no page claims otherwise. A truly tick-level feed needs the WebSocket API, whose handshake requires a key. Observed supporting evidence the same day: GET /markets?tickers=KXAAAGASM-26NOV30-3.90 returned last_price_dollars 0.7500 with updated_time 2026-10-27T20:34:13Z and volume_24h_fp '0.00'.

facts.claim: When `tickers` is the ONLY filter, GET /markets returns every matching market in one response and ignores `limit`
facts.value: Every matching market is returned in one response, in no guaranteed order; `limit` is not applied and the returned cursor is empty.
facts.how: Read in the official Paging and ordering section this session. The chat dock relies on exactly this: it sends only repeated `tickers=` parameters and therefore needs no paging loop. A live call with one ticker returned {"cursor":"","markets":[...]} as documented.

facts.claim: Unauthenticated public requests have separate, undocumented limits; clients must back off on 429
facts.value: Not quantified by Kalshi ('subject to separate limits'). Back off on 429.
facts.how: Read this session. Because no number is published, the chat dock polls slowly (12 s) and pauses while the tab is hidden rather than claiming a safe rate.
